name: Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195) - Kernel Race Condition Privesc
description: Dirty COW (Copy-On-Write) is a race condition in the Linux kernel memory subsystem that allows writing to read-only memory mappings. It affects kernels 2.x through 4.x (patched in 4.8.3). The most reliable variants overwrite /etc/passwd to add a root user or replace SUID binaries. Still commonly found on older/unpatched systems and CTF boxes.
notes:
=== AFFECTED KERNELS ===
Linux kernel 2.x through 4.8.2
Patched in 4.8.3 (October 2016)
Check: uname -r

=== VARIANT 1: /etc/passwd overwrite (most reliable) ===
  # dirty.c / dirtycow-mem.c
  gcc -pthread dirty.c -o dirty -lcrypt
  ./dirty <new_password>
  # Adds user "firefart" with root UID and your password
  su firefart

=== VARIANT 2: SUID binary replacement ===
  # cowroot.c - replaces /usr/bin/passwd with a root shell
  gcc -pthread cowroot.c -o cowroot
  ./cowroot

=== VARIANT 3: Write to arbitrary file ===
  # pokemon.c - write arbitrary content to any file
  gcc -pthread pokemon.c -o pokemon
  ./pokemon <target_file>

=== STABILITY WARNING ===
Dirty COW exploits a kernel race condition. They can:
- Crash the kernel (panic)
- Corrupt memory
- Hang the system
Always try the /etc/passwd variant first - its most stable.
Do NOT use in production without explicit authorization.

=== DOWNLOAD ===
  # Multiple variants at:
  # https://github.com/dirtycow/dirtycow.github.io/wiki/PoCs

examples.label: Compile and run passwd overwrite variant

references.title: MITRE T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

recommended.note: LES identifies Dirty COW among other kernel exploits.
DirtyPipe is the modern successor to DirtyCOW (kernel 5.8+).

defense.why_it_works: A race condition between the madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) and write system calls allows a non-privileged process to modify read-only memory mappings, including files owned by root.
defense.prerequisites: Linux kernel 2.x-4.8.2; ability to compile and execute code on the target.
defense.impact: Root privilege escalation by overwriting /etc/passwd or replacing SUID binaries.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1068] Compilation activity (gcc); /etc/passwd modification; unexpected SUID changes.
defense.artifacts: File modification of /etc/passwd; new user "firefart"; gcc compilation; core dumps from race condition.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux sourcetype=linux_audit (key="passwd_changes" OR key="suid_changes" OR (syscall="execve" AND exe="/usr/bin/gcc"))
| table _time, host, auid, key, exe
defense.sentinel_kql:
Syslog
| where SyslogMessage has "/etc/passwd" or (ProcessName == "gcc" and SyslogMessage has "-pthread")
| project TimeGenerated, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
defense.prevention: Patch kernel to 4.8.3+; remove compiler (gcc) from production systems; monitor /etc/passwd integrity; use SELinux/AppArmor.

detections.name: Dirty COW exploitation indicators
detections.logic:
title: Dirty COW Kernel Exploit Indicators
status: experimental
logsource:
  product: linux
  service: auditd
detection:
  selection_compile:
    key: software_mgmt
    exe|endswith: /gcc
    a0|contains: -pthread
  selection_passwd:
    key: passwd_changes
    nametype: NORMAL
  condition: selection_compile or selection_passwd
level: critical
detections.false_positives: Legitimate compilation on development systems; authorized password changes
detections.tuning: Critical alert on production systems; reduce to high on dev systems
